theme: Feeling behind: Nora, 19, stays home and works the 5 a.m. bakery shift while friends move away; her receipt sketches of the regulars become a sketchbook and a wall
hook: At nineteen, Nora felt behind in life.

lines.text: At nineteen, Nora felt behind in life.
This is a story about her, and a stack of old receipts.
That fall, her friends posted move-in days and new cities.
Nora worked the five a.m. shift at a small bakery.
The ovens were the only warm light on the street.
She knew every regular by their order.
The nurse who wanted the burnt end. The old man who paid in coins.
On slow mornings, she sketched them on the backs of receipts and hid them in her apron.
One morning, the old man saw a drawing of himself.
He looked at it for a long time, then asked to keep it.
The next week, he brought her a sketchbook.
Nora kept going, one regular at a time.
By the next fall, the book was full, and the bakery had a wall of her drawings.
People came in just to find themselves.
Nora was still at home, still up at five.
But for the first time, her life felt like it had already started.
If you're the one still at home, look around. Your road might already be under your feet.

post.caption: Feeling behind in life when everyone else moved away. A short story about Nora, a 5 a.m. bakery and a stack of receipts. What are you quietly getting good at? 🥐
post.pinned_comment: If you drew the regulars in your life, who'd be first? 👇
